ai.description: This globular frog reaches 3–4 cm. It is dark brown with irregular yellow-orange mottling. Key features include a rounded snout, short limbs, and specialized shovel-like metatarsal tubercles for digging.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uperodon anamalaiensis* is best distinguished by the presence of distinct, bright yellow or orange spots on its dark brown to blackish dorsal skin.
ai.habitat: The Anamalai globular frog inhabits leaf litter in moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Anamalai Globular Frog is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending much of its time buried underground to retain moisture in its humid forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uperodon anamalaiensis* breeds during the monsoon, laying large clutches of eggs in temporary rain pools. It exhibits an explosive breeding mode typical of microhylids.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Anamalai globular frog is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically occurring at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Anamalai Globular Frog emits a series of short, high-pitched "peep" notes, typically heard during the monsoon season from flooded forest floors or leaf litter.
